cr_data.provenance:
Artist's collection. 
The Downtown Gallery, Nueva York, a partir de 1950. [Label on verso. As "Shell & Shingle no.6", nº 143] 
Mr. John Marin, Jr. (1915-1988) y Norma Boom Marin, Maplewood, NJ, 1958. [inscripción en protección trasera, “Collection Mr. & Mrs. John Marin, Jr.”, as ""Shell & Shingle #6"Private collection, Orano, ME, 1979. 
Kennedy Galleries, Inc., Nueva York. [Label on verso. As "Shell & Shingle #6", stock no. 213128.1] 
Thyssen-Bornemisza Collection, Lugano, 1980. 
On loan at the Museo Thyssen-Bornemisza, Madrid, 1992. 
Museo Thyssen-Bornemisza, Madrid, 1993. 
(Source: Museo Nacional Thyssen-Bornemisza, 2026)
remarks_1999: V in first title written in by Doris Bry in black ink in Abiquiú Notebooks. Whitney Archive indicates, "Exam. at Amer. Place, April 1945 [notes stretcher inscription 1]. . . . Similar but less abstract than the Fischel picture –– shingle does not reach top of picture. Slate grey shingle with small white shell at base. Pale grey background." Abiquiú Notebooks after 1977 notes stretcher inscription 1. Part of series renumbered by O'Keeffe and Doris Bry in 1970. (Source: Lynes, 1999)

titles.notes: Source of title: Downtown Gallery Archive.
titles.title: Shell & Shingle No. 6

description: A bright white shell sits on a black surface. Just behind the shell, a gray single stands on its side against a white wall. The details of both the shell and shingle have been omitted, giving the work a semiabstract appearance.
title: Shell and Old Shingle V
